user.title: How does Home Assistant reach your panel?
user.description:
Most people have a **SmartCom** (the box the Texecom app uses): choose **Texecom Connect**.

Choose **Crestron** only if one of the panel's COM ports is set to *Crestron System* and you reach it through a serial-to-network adapter or a cable.

connect.title: Your SmartCom
connect.description:
Find the SmartCom in your router's list of devices and reserve its address so it never changes.

Home Assistant uses the SmartCom's connection for the Texecom app, so the app can't connect while Home Assistant is: your alarm and the app's alarm notifications work as before. If Homebridge or texecom2mqtt use the SmartCom, turn them off first.

Connecting can take up to a minute.

Need help? See the [setup guide]({help}).

data_description.port: Leave at 10001 unless your installer changed it.
data_description.udl: The panel's remote-access code (not your keypad code). Texecom's default is 1234, and most panels keep it.

crestron.title: How is the Crestron port connected?

menu_options.crestron_network: Over the network (an adapter or a SmartCom in Crestron mode)
menu_options.crestron_serial: Serial cable or USB adapter on this machine

crestron_network.title: Crestron over the network
crestron_network.description: The COM port must be set to **Crestron System** in Wintex or at the keypad. See [using a Crestron port]({help}) for how it differs from Texecom Connect.

data_description.udl: Needed to arm and disarm from Home Assistant. Leave empty for sensors only.
data_description.zone_count: Crestron can't read zone names: zones appear as "Zone 1", "Zone 2"… and you can rename them in Home Assistant.

crestron_serial.title: Crestron over a serial cable
crestron_serial.description: The COM port must be set to **Crestron System** in Wintex or at the keypad. See [using a Crestron port]({help}) for how it differs from Texecom Connect.

data_description.baud_rate: As set for the COM port (often 19200).
data_description.udl: Needed to arm and disarm from Home Assistant. Leave empty for sensors only.
data_description.zone_count: Zones appear as "Zone 1", "Zone 2"… and you can rename them in Home Assistant.

data.create_dashboard: Add an 'Alarm' dashboard to the sidebar

data_description.create_dashboard: Built from Home Assistant's own cards: the alarm with its arm buttons, recent activity, and every zone grouped by type. You can edit or delete it like any dashboard.

arm_modes_crestron.title: Arm modes
arm_modes_crestron.description:
**'Away'** always arms the whole alarm. Choose the part arm behind **'Night'** and **'Home'**, or *'Not used'* to hide that button. Over Crestron, part arms work for area 1 only. Unsure? See [part arms explained]({help}).

Crestron doesn't say whether the panel was fully or part armed when it's set at the keypad: choose how that should show.

reauth_confirm.title: The panel refused the UDL code
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the panel's current UDL code (your installer can tell you if it was changed). Checking it can take up to a minute.

reconfigure.title: Change the connection
reconfigure.description: Home Assistant pauses its connection to the panel while it checks the new details.

data_description.udl: Needed to arm and disarm from Home Assistant. Leave empty for sensors only.

reconfigure_connect.title: Change the connection
reconfigure_connect.description: For example after the SmartCom's address changed, or a new UDL code. Home Assistant pauses its connection to the panel while it checks: this can take up to a minute.

error.cannot_connect: Couldn't connect. Check the address and port. If the Texecom app, Homebridge or texecom2mqtt was connected a moment ago, wait a minute and try again.
error.invalid_auth: The panel refused the UDL code.
error.invalid_udl: The UDL code is 4 to 8 digits.
error.no_zones: Connected, but the panel reported no zones in use.
error.no_reply: Connected, but the panel didn't answer. Check the COM port is set to Crestron System and the speed matches.
error.same_part_arm: Night and Home can't use the same part arm.
error.cannot_open_serial: Couldn't open that serial device. Check the path (a /dev/serial/by-id/… path survives restarts) and that nothing else is using it.

abort.already_configured: This panel is already set up.

progress.connecting:
Logging in to your panel and reading its zones and areas.

This usually takes about ten seconds, or up to a minute if something else (the Texecom app, Homebridge, a restart) was connected to the SmartCom just before.

alarm_code.title: Home Assistant alarm code
alarm_code.description: A code Home Assistant asks for before disarming. It's checked by Home Assistant, not the panel, and has nothing to do with your keypad codes. Leave it empty for no code.

data.code_arm_required: Ask for the code when arming too

data_description.code_arm_required: If you use Apple Home, the HomeKit Bridge then needs the code in its settings too, or arming from the Home app fails.

user_names.title: Names for keypad users
user_names.description:
When someone uses a keypad, the alarm says who: *changed by User 3*. Give users names to see *changed by Sam* instead.

One user per line, the number then the name, for example:
`1 = Sam`
`3 = Alex`

The numbers are the ones your installer gave each code.

notices.title: Notifications
notices.description: Home Assistant can show a notification while something needs attention. It goes by itself once it's put right.

data.notify_mains: When the panel loses mains power
data.notify_tamper: When a tamper opens (the panel's lid, a detector's cover, the bell box…)

clock.title: Panel clock
clock.description:
The panel's clock resets if it loses all power (mains and battery). Home Assistant can keep it right: it checks once a day and when it connects, using Home Assistant's time zone, and sets it if it's more than a minute out.

Saving reconnects to the panel, which can take up to a minute.

status_poll.title: Checking the panel
status_poll.description:
How often Home Assistant asks the panel whether it's armed. It corrects missed events, and reconnects if the panel goes quiet. 0 turns it off.

Saving reconnects to the panel.

dashboard.title: Create or refresh the Alarm dashboard
dashboard.description: Builds the Alarm dashboard from the current zones and puts it in the sidebar. If you already have it, any changes you made to it are replaced.

progress.reading: Reading the zones and areas from the panel. This takes about ten seconds.

error.same_part_arm: Night and Home can't use the same part arm.
error.invalid_user_names: Use one user per line, the number then the name, like `3 = Sam`.

abort.rediscovered: Read the panel again. Zones in use: {zones}. Areas: {areas}. Home Assistant reconnects to use them, which can take up to a minute.
abort.rediscover_failed: Couldn't read the panel just now (it may be busy, e.g. reporting an alarm). Try again in a minute.
abort.dashboard_created: The Alarm dashboard is ready: it's in the sidebar.
abort.dashboard_failed: Couldn't create the dashboard on this version of Home Assistant. [Build the dashboard yourself]({help}) has a version you can paste in.

command_failed.message: The panel didn't accept the request: {error}

not_connected.message: Home Assistant isn't connected to the panel just now. It reconnects by itself, so try again in a minute. Panel connection, on the panel's device, shows the link.

refused.message: The panel refused. The keypad usually shows why, for example a fault, a tamper, or something that needs attention.

panel_clock_wrong.title: Your alarm panel's clock is wrong

confirm.title: Set the panel's clock
confirm.description:
The panel's clock is {drift}, usually because it lost all power (mains and battery). Its event log, and any timed arming your installer set up, use that clock.

Click **Submit** to turn on **Keep the panel clock right**: Home Assistant sets the clock now, using its own time zone, and checks it once a day.

panel_offline.title: Can't reach {name}
panel_offline.description:
Home Assistant hasn't been able to connect to the alarm panel at **{address}** for {minutes} minutes ({error}).

Check that the SmartCom (or adapter) is powered and on the network, and that its address hasn't changed: reserve it in your router. If it moved, use **Reconfigure** on the Texecom integration. Also check nothing else is connected to it (the Texecom app, Homebridge, texecom2mqtt).

This notice clears itself once the panel is back. [What to check]({help})
